title: Plane Geometry
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Pre-Technical Studies; not yet checked by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher; safety lines marked SAFETY in the library to confirm first; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Constructing combined shapes (outcome c) is marked on the learner's drawing with the rubric; the questions test the construction steps.

skills.key_step: The learner names the instruments used in technical drawing and their jobs: drawing board, T-square (horizontal lines), set squares 45 and 30-60 degrees (vertical and angled lines), compass and dividers (circles and arcs, stepping off), protractor (angles), scale rule, pencils (grades H, HB), eraser, French curves.

floor.question: Which line shows the outline of an object?

representations: an instrument and job matching chart
a board with a T-square and set squares
steps: Use it to draw one line.

board.do: Draw a T-square on a board and two set squares.

board.say: Which angles can you draw with it on the T-square?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say 30, 60 and 90 degrees.

misconceptions.repair: Match each instrument to one job on the board; draw a circle with a compass and an angle with a set square.
Slide the T-square stock along the board edge and draw parallel horizontal lines; set squares rest on it for angles.
Measure a corner with the protractor and a side with a rule; one gives degrees, the other millimetres.

misconceptions.ask: Which set square draws a 60 degree line?
misconceptions.repair: Hold up both set squares, read the angles at their corners, and draw 30, 45 and 60 degree lines on the T-square.

skills.key_step: The learner explains the layout of a drawing environment: board and T-square on the working edge, paper fixed square with tape, sheet sizes (A4 297 x 210 mm, A3 420 x 297 mm), a border inside the edges, the title block at the bottom right (title, name, scale, date, units), good light and a tidy space.

floor.prerequisite: Can print in capitals between guide lines.
floor.question: How are notes printed on a drawing?

representations: a laid-out A4 sheet with border and title block
a photo of a drawing desk
steps: Fix the paper square to the board.
Draw the title block at the bottom right.
contexts: a workshop drawing pinned to a wall

board.do: Point at the bottom right corner.
board.say: What goes here, and what is written in it?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say the title block: title, name, scale, date.
Draw the border and title block.

misconceptions.ask: Where is the title block of a drawing sheet?
misconceptions.repair: Look at a real drawing sheet: the title block is at the bottom right, where it can be read when sheets are folded or filed.

listen_for: It is not needed; the paper edge is enough
misconceptions.ask: Why is a border drawn on a drawing sheet?
misconceptions.repair: Draw a border 10 mm inside the edges; explain it frames the drawing and leaves a margin for handling and filing.

misconceptions.ask: What is the size of A4?
misconceptions.repair: Fold an A3 sheet in half: it makes two A4 sheets. Measure: A4 is 297 by 210 mm.

misconceptions.ask: Along which edge of the drawing board does the stock of the T-square slide?
misconceptions.repair: Show that only one edge is kept true; using others gives lines that are not parallel.

checks.question: Where is the title block on a drawing sheet?
What is the size of A4?

skills.key_step: The learner gives and follows the steps for constructions used in combined shapes: bisect a line, construct 60, 90, 30 and 45 degree angles, a hexagon in a circle (side equals radius), and a slot or rounded rectangle (centres on the centre line, radius half the width); the drawing is marked with the rubric.

floor.question: Which instrument draws circles and arcs?

representations: a step-by-step bisection on the board
a hexagon stepped round a circle
a slot with its centre line and centres marked
steps: Draw the base line or centre line.
Set the compass to the right radius.
Join the points and firm the outline.
contexts: setting out a right angle for a garden bed

board.do: Draw a circle of radius 30 mm.
Point at the compass set to 30 mm.
board.say: How many times will this step round the circle, and what shape do we get?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say six times, a hexagon.
Step it round and join the points.

misconceptions.ask: A regular hexagon is drawn in a circle of radius 30 mm. How long is each side?
misconceptions.repair: Step the compass round the circle at the radius: it fits exactly six times. Join the points.

misconceptions.ask: To bisect a line AB with a compass, the radius must be...
misconceptions.repair: Try both on the board: arcs with a short radius do not cross. Use a radius clearly more than half.

misconceptions.ask: A slot is 20 mm wide with semicircular ends. What radius draws each end?
misconceptions.repair: Draw the centre line, mark the two centres on it, and set the compass to half the width.

listen_for: It cannot be; a protractor is needed
misconceptions.ask: How is a 60 degree angle constructed with a compass and a ruler?
misconceptions.repair: Construct 60 degrees with equal arcs and check it with a protractor; the two agree.

checks.question: When bisecting a line, how wide is the compass set?
What radius draws the ends of a 20 mm wide slot?
